item.title: OSC700: A GW+BSE Dataset of 700 Organic Semiconductor (OSC) Crystals with an LLM-Assisted Data Extraction Agent
item.description:
Key parameters for organic optoelectronic device applications derive from the excited-state properties of molecular crystals. Data scarcity (both experimental and theoretical) limits the ability to train machine learning (ML) models to predict these properties. We present the OSC700 dataset of excited-state properties of 700 crystalline organic semiconductors (OSCs) with up to 1168 atoms in the unit cell, calculated using state-of-the-art many-body perturbation theory within the GW approximation and Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW+BSE). OSC700 contains crystals of compounds comprising C,H,N,O,F,S capable of forming a variety of molecular scaffolds and crystal packing motifs. OSC700 is larger and significantly more diverse than the earlier PAH101 dataset [Scientific Data 12, 679 (2025)]. The data records contain the fundamental gap, quasiparticle band structure, static dielectric constant, first singlet exciton energy (optical gap), first triplet exciton energy, full dielectric function, and optical absorption spectra for light polarized along the three lattice vectors. Because absorption experiments on molecular crystals are rare (as opposed to solution or amorphous phases), we developed an LLM-assisted data extraction agent in order to find and retrieve available optical gap data for the materials in OSC700. The agent was able to find experimental data for 16 materials, which we used to validate the results of our calculations. The OSC700 dataset can be used to train ML models to predict the excited-state properties of crystalline organic semiconductors and find promising materials for optoelectronic device applications.

Yiqun Luo, Xuyan Chen, Siyu Chen, Kaiji Zhao, Filippo Simini, Mauro DelBen, Noa Marom

item.title: Chemistry-Informed Transfer and Interaction-Resolved Learning Towards Data-Efficient Materials Exploration
item.description:
Optimizing synthesis parameters for new thin-film materials is slow and often relies on intuition and trial and error. Gaussian process (GP) models suit low-data settings, but treat each material separately or need engineered descriptors to learn across materials. Multi-task GPs share information across materials but infer these relationships solely from sparse data, making them unreliable early on. We introduce a chemistry-informed multi-task GP that derives these relationships from a Tanimoto kernel on molecular fingerprints, enabling knowledge transfer without descriptor engineering. In closed-loop, uncertaintydriven exploration of a seven-dimensional synthesis space, comprising one categorical variable (three chiral 2D hybrid organic-inorganic perovskite compositions) and six continuous synthesis parameters, we tested 287 conditions (<0.1% of the discretized synthesis space). Knowledge transfer matched the accuracy of single-task GPs trained on the full target dataset using between 35-60% of the target data. Interaction analysis revealed a three-way coupling among annealing temperature, precursor concentration, and composition. This coupling makes a one-variable-at-a-time optimization challenging. Our framework offers a simple strategy for transferring and interpreting knowledge across related materials.

Yi-Ru Liu, Maher B. Alghalayini, Do-Kyoung Lee, Marcus M. Noack, Larry Lüer, Christoph J. Brabec, Carolin M. Sutter-Fella

item.title: vibyverse: an integrated computational chemistry ecosystem developed through agentic engineering
item.description:
We describe the vibyverse, developed by agentic engineering, comprising vibe-sketcher for chemical structures and reaction schemes, vibe-qc for electronic-structure calculations, vibe-scheduler for execution and retrieval, vibe-viewer for inspection and presentation, and the Quantum Visualization Format (QVF) for structured exchange. The workflow starts with reaction design in vibe-sketcher, submission through vibe-scheduler, calculation with vibe-qc, and inspection and analysis in vibe-viewer, with scientific data transferred through QVF. We examine the responsibilities of each component and the information that must survive their connections, including charge, multiplicity, geometry, method settings, runtime identity and result provenance. Source inspection identifies implemented interfaces and their compatibility requirements. A Diels–Alder preparation example connects an editable scheme and preoptimized structures to validated QVF and viewer exports. The executed numerical workflow proceeds through MACE geometry optimization, PBE/def2-SVP refinement and DLPNO-CCSD(T) endpoint energies. A proposed water-on-boronnitride example would extend the workflow to periodic structures. The molecular optimization and Hessian use existing PBE routes without an added dispersion correction. Both Hessian stencils identify minima for all three molecules. With an explicit restrictedreference contract, the correlated electronic energy of cyclohexene relative to butadiene and ethene is −190.547 kJ mol−1. Changing from TightPNO to NormalPNO shifts it by +0.187 kJ mol−1. The viewer reproduces both electronic reaction energies from the archived endpoints, in agreement with an independent stoichiometric sum. All data supporting this study are openly available from the Zenodo repository under accession number 23976098 at https://zenodo.org/records/23976098.

Michael F. Peintinger

item.title: Advanced High-Throughput Characterization of Nanoporous Materials using Pore Graphs
item.description:
Nanoporous materials databases now contain millions of structures, yet the tools for characterizing their void spaces have not kept pace. Standard descriptors such as largest cavity diameter and pore limiting diameter are global quantities that conflate local pore geometry with inter-pore connectivity, and can hide distinct pores and network topology behind a single number. We present Mofography, an open-source Python/Rust library that recasts pore characterization as a three-dimensional image-processing problem. It segments the void space into non-overlapping pore regions, connects them at shared windows, and constructs a pore graph that decouples local properties (size, shape, chemistry) from global topology (percolation, connectivity). Global textural properties are obtained as queries on this graph and agree with those from Zeo++ and Pore-Blazer across a diverse set of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), while remaining traceable to individual pores and windows. The same representation supports pore-resolved pore size distributions, multi-modal pore-type clustering, window detection across periodic boundaries, and percolation and accessibility analysis. To demonstrate its utility for material discovery, we develop a workflow integrated with Mofography to screen favorable pores in MOFs for xylene isomer separations and validate selected candidates with grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations. The results reveal how accessibility and competing pore environments influence whether local preferences translate into material performance. By linking global textural properties to local pore environments and their connectivity, Mofography provides a unique platform for interpreting structure–property relationships and accelerating nanoporous materials discovery.

Arun Gopalan, Chao Zheng, Behnam Azadpour, Kaihang Shi, Lev Sarkisov

item.title: Training of Neural Network Machine Learning Potentials for Activation Barrier Calculations in Predicting Growth Modes of Deposited Metals
item.description:
Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are opening many new opportunities to extend the capabilities of computational materials science. MLIPs deliver increased throughput and simulations at time and length scales beyond first principles density functional theory (DFT), while maintaining near-DFT accuracy, thus allowing unravelling of chemical processes not accessible with DFT. In this work, we present an approach to training a neural network MLIP using DeepMD-kit software that delivers both accurate energies and forces, suitable for determining activation energies via nudged elastic band calculations. We use the deposition of metals on substrates, in particular Ru and Cu on TaN for semiconductor device interconnects, as the example system, for which activation barriers of metal atom migration at the metal-substrate interface and on the metal deposit are important in understanding the evolution of the film morphology during deposition. The structure of the metal-substrate interface directly affects the performance of devices, from catalysts and sensors, to interconnects and contacts in nanoelectronics. The activation barrier energies from our MLIP for all sizes of metal atom deposits reproduce the DFT activation energies to within an average error of 0.08 eV (6%) for Cu and 0.23 eV (19%) for Ru. The trends of the DFT barriers are preserved by the MLIP and the computing time is reduced from days using high performance computing to minutes on a personal laptop. This allows us to assess the activation energies for complex processes such as the transition of a 2-layer metal cluster to a 3-layer cluster-a key step in metal island growth. Morphology evolution occurs on multiple scales, from initial nucleation, to layer growth and cluster ripening. By demonstrating that MLIPs can be used to accurately and rapidly deliver activation energies for the relevant atomic scale processes, a multi-scale predictive atomistic model of metal deposition and growth chemistry becomes feasible.

Karl Rönnby, Cara-Lena Nies, Savannah May Timony, Michael Nolan, Nolan Michael

item.title: Mechanosensitive ion transport in hexagonal boron nitride nanopores
item.description:
In biological systems, mechanical strain can trigger strong changes in ion conductance and signaling, yet in synthetic nanopores, achieving similar mechanosensitive behavior has been a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that subtle mechanical strain can induce strong modulation of ionic current in small hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) nanopores. Using hydrostatic pressure to apply small lateral strain to free-standing single-layer h-BN membranes featuring triangular sub-1-nm nanopores, we observed ion conductance modulation exceeding 1 30% under 0.5% strain. We attribute this response to the strain-dependent interplay of ionpore and ion-water interactions within the nanopore. The measured mechanosensitivity values also agreed strongly with those obtained from modeling of strain-tunable transport in ensembles of h-BN nanopores. These findings establish a framework for developing strain-responsive membranes for applications in molecular separations and sensing.

Mohit Saraswat, Yechan Noh, Alex T. Hall, Dana O. Byrne, Karina Damberg, Sanjin Marion, Camille A. Violet, Julia Chung, John Cumings, Aleksandra Radenovic, Frances I. Allen, Alex Smolyanitsky, Aleksandr Noy
